title: Biocentric/gutportrait pipeline parameters
description: Cross-cohort comparison of personal 16S gut microbiome profiles against co-processed reference panels

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to a comma-separated samplesheet with one row per sample in the ampliseq run: the personal samples and every reference-panel sample.
input.help_text: Required columns: `sample`, `role` (personal or panel), `study`, `run`. Optional: `age_cat`, `sex`, `bmi_cat`, `country`. Sample names must match the columns of the ampliseq ASV table. `run` should be the sequencing flowcell, because it is the unit DADA2's error model is learned on. See docs/usage.md.

ampliseq_results.description: Path to an nf-core/ampliseq results directory.
ampliseq_results.help_text: gutportrait reads `dada2/ASV_table.tsv` and the named-rank taxonomy `dada2/ASV_tax_species.<taxonomy_db>.tsv` from it. The personal and panel samples should come from ONE ampliseq run, so they share an error model and an ASV space: co-processing beats batch correction.

taxonomy_db.description: Reference database ampliseq classified against; selects `ASV_tax_species.<taxonomy_db>.tsv`.
taxonomy_db.help_text: SILVA 138.2 is the default for the native V3-V4 arm: on the validation data it gave genus calls for 79% of ASVs against 49% for ampliseq's SBDI-GTDB default.

arm.description: Which comparison arm this run is: native V3-V4, or V4-projected.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

analysis_options.title: Analysis options
analysis_options.description: Thresholds for positioning. Defaults are deliberately strict (DECISIONS.md D10).

min_panel_samples.description: Minimum number of panel samples required to compute percentiles.

min_prevalence.description: Keep genera present in at least this fraction of PANEL samples.
min_prevalence.help_text: Applied to the panel only; filtering on the personal samples would select features for being present in you, which is circular.

pseudocount.description: Additive pseudocount applied before the centred-log-ratio transform.

min_study_n.description: Panel studies with fewer samples are left out of per-study bounds and PERMANOVA models.

seed.description: Random seed for rarefaction and permutation tests, so every run is reproducible.

rarefaction_depth.description: Reads per sample for alpha diversity. Samples below it get no alpha diversity and are listed.
rarefaction_depth.help_text: Observed richness grows with depth, so every sample is subsampled to the same depth before alpha diversity is computed.

banner_r2_study.description: If study explains more than this share of panel variance (R2), every population claim is flagged orientation only.

deviation_options.title: Deviation flag options
deviation_options.description: Thresholds for the extremes-only deviation flags (DECISIONS.md D12). Strict by default.

flag_low_percentile.description: A low value must fall below this percentile of the pooled panel and of every panel study.

flag_high_percentile.description: A high value must exceed this percentile of the pooled panel and of every panel study.

dominance_threshold.description: Flag a single genus above this fraction of the sample.

core_prevalence.description: Genera present in at least this fraction of the panel count as core.

core_min_expected.description: A missing core genus is flagged only if the panel median predicts at least this many reads at the sample's depth.

gate_options.title: Batch correction and gate options
gate_options.description: Batch correction of the panel and the two gates of DECISIONS.md D12. Strict by default.

correction_covariates.description: Comma-separated samplesheet columns to protect during batch correction, e.g. "age_cat,sex". Columns not filled for every panel sample are dropped and listed.

pc_fold.description: Positive control: fold change planted in half of each panel study.

pc_alpha.description: Positive control: the planted effect must survive correction at this significance (paired Wilcoxon).

pc_retain.description: Positive control: share of the planted CLR shift that must survive correction. Below it, the run stops.

pc_min_prevalence.description: Positive control: the planted genus is chosen among genera present in at least this fraction of the panel.

dominance_alpha.description: Batch dominance: a contrast counts as a finding only if its R2 exceeds R2(study) and p is below this.

stability_low_percentile.description: Stability: genus positions at or below this percentile count as low.

stability_high_percentile.description: Stability: genus positions at or above this percentile count as high.

qc_max_z.description: Technical comparability: a read-retention metric is atypical when its modified z-score against the panel, and against every panel study, is beyond this on its worse side.

within_person_options.title: Within-person change and identity options
within_person_options.description: How changes between the personal samples are judged against the within-person variation of panel people sampled twice (samplesheet role repeat).

change_z.description: A genus changed between two personal samples when its CLR change exceeds this many times its ordinary within-person change.

min_reference_pairs.description: Fewer panel repeat pairs than this: no within-person reference is used, and the change statistics are not assessable.

identity_within_percentile.description: Identity: a distance at or below this percentile of the within-person pairs is ordinary for one person.

identity_between_percentile.description: Identity: a distance below this percentile of the pairs of different people is ordinary for one person.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
